name: Validation core types
purpose: Define the closed, bounded vocabulary shared by every T025 component: identifiers, timestamps, result codes, diagnostics, actions, lifecycle states, and the field-locator enum.
responsibilities: Define bounded value types (clock domain id, timestamp, permit id, session id, controller id, manager scope, generation, nonce, plan digest, tags, quotas) with explicit width and maximum length.
Define the closed Action bit enum, the ActionMask type, and the rule that undefined bits and non-explicit composites are invalid.
Define the LifecycleState enum (declared, armed, active, closing, closed, expired, revoked, evidence_incomplete) with an explicit terminal-state predicate.
Define the Result enum (all deterministic outcomes) and the payload-free Diagnostic type holding an ordered code sequence plus at most one bounded numeric locator.
Define the fixed FieldLocator enum used to name the mismatching permit field in a PermitMismatch diagnostic.

Provide a canonical, deterministic, standard-library-only byte-serialization and FNV-1a 128-bit content digest used for permit identity; documented as a local bookkeeping identity, not a cryptographic claim.
state_ownership: None. This component is a pure value/type layer with no shared mutable state and no object identity.
interfaces: types: ClockDomainId, Timestamp, Tolerance, Generation, Nonce, PlanDigest, SessionId, ControllerId, ManagerScope, Tag, Quota, QuotaKind, Action, ActionMask, LifecycleState, Result, FieldLocator, Diagnostic, PermitId
concurrency: Not applicable. All types are immutable or trivially copyable values; they are safe to share across threads by value without synchronization.
errors: No runtime errors; all value invariants are enforced by construction-time validation in the owning components.
deployment: Header-only within the xverse::xcom::validation namespace; compiled as part of the standalone candidate, no external dependency beyond the C++20 standard library.
rationale: A single closed vocabulary prevents silent cross-domain timestamp comparison, keeps diagnostics payload-free, and gives later trace links a stable anchor for every enum and value type.
